sources.entry: A low-code development platform (LCDP) provides a development environment used to create application software through a graphical user interface.

summary.name: Low-code development platform
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing low-code development platforms (LCDPs), software environments that use mainly graphical interfaces so applications can be built with little or no hand-written code.
use_cases: Building business applications faster with less coding
Letting non-developers contribute to app development
Creating mobile and multi-device apps without separate coding
Automating business processes with custom software
Evaluating low-code platforms for enterprise use
summary.what_it_does: The page defines low-code development platforms as environments, typically graphical, that involve little or no code and may produce fully working applications or require added code for special cases. It traces their roots to 1990s and early 2000s rapid application development tools and fourth-generation languages, and says they rely on model-driven architecture, automatic code generation, and visual programming. It covers market context, including a 2016 Forrester estimate of a $15.5 billion market by 2020, and lists criticisms such as doubts about suitability for large mission-critical systems and risks of shadow IT. It is a general encyclopedia overview, not a page for a specific product.
notable: Traces the concept to 4GL and rapid application development tools
The name 'low-code' was introduced in 2014 by Forrester Research
Notes governance and security concerns, including shadow IT
caveats: Criticized for uncertain suitability for large-scale, mission-critical enterprise applications
Some question whether these platforms really make development cheaper or easier
Security and compliance concerns are growing, especially for apps using consumer data
